newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks slip at open, golds dive.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks slip at open, golds dive.

text.p: Australian shares slipped at the open on Friday, Thursday afternoon's fade continuing as gold stocks tracked the metal's price lower and bellwether BHP suffered further modest selling after a strong week.

From a low on November 14 of A$16.88 (US$13.70) BHP gained 8.6 percent to a five-month high of A$18.34 in Thursday's record-breaking opening session. It opened on Thursday at A$18.13, off two cents from Thursday's close.
From the opening, the All Ordinaries index lost 10.0 points to 2,382.5.

The gold index lost over 1.5 percent in early trade after gold lost its lustre offshore as central bank selling rumours overhung the market. The slide was exacerbated by the strength of the Australian dollar and South African rand which encouraged producer hedging.

"Golds are well off and most of the rest are a bit softer but we have had a good run, BHP particularly," said a Sydney-based dealer, adding that banking sector was still racking up gains after some well-received profit results.
"The banks are still very strong, National Australia Bank and ANZ Bank are both higher."
As with many others, the dealer suggested the near-term outlook was still positive with a retracement from Thursday's record highs not a major cause for concern.
"We still see it higher by January assuming there is no drama in the U.S.," the dealer said.
Falls outnumbered rises by a ratio of about eight to five, while about 42 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
